title: Units and counits for restriction of an adjunction through completion reflectors
statement:
Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B$ be additive $A$-linear categories for a commutative ring $A$ [def-weil-linear-category]. Let $\mathcal A_c,\mathcal B_c$ be full additive subcategories, and let $C_{\mathcal A},C_{\mathcal B}$ be additive $A$-linear endofunctors with values in those subcategories. Suppose natural maps $\kappa_X:X\to C(X)$ have the following universal property: for every object $Y$ of the indicated subcategory, precomposition by $\kappa_X$ is a bijection $\operatorname{Hom}(C(X),Y)\to\operatorname{Hom}(X,Y)$. Assume the subcategories consist exactly of the objects with invertible $\kappa$. Let $L:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ and $R:\mathcal B\to\mathcal A$ be additive $A$-linear functors with a specified adjunction $L\dashv R$, unit $\eta$ and counit $\varepsilon$, and assume $R(\mathcal B_c)\subseteq\mathcal A_c$. Define $P=C_{\mathcal B}L|_{\mathcal A_c}$ and $D=R|_{\mathcal B_c}$.
There is an $A$-linear natural adjunction bijection
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal B_c}(PM,N)\xrightarrow{\ -\circ\kappa_{LM}\ }\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal B}(LM,N)\xrightarrow{\operatorname{adj}}\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A_c}(M,DN).$$
The resulting unit $\eta^c$ and counit $\varepsilon^c$ satisfy, as ambient morphisms,
$$\eta^c_M=R(\kappa_{LM})\eta_M,\qquad \varepsilon^c_N\kappa_{LRN}=\varepsilon_N.$$
They are natural and satisfy both triangle identities. More generally the ordinary adjunct of $t\kappa_{LM}$ equals the completed adjunct of every $t:PM\to N$. The functors $P,D$ are additive and $A$-linear. These statements fix the adjunction by its Hom bijection, rather than merely asserting existence of some adjunction.

source.place: Tag 099K, lemma-pushforward-derived-complete-adjoint, final Hom bijection; abstract scalar and unit/counit refinement, agent supplied

proof.text: All compositions below are read right to left. Full subcategories have the ambient Hom modules and composition. The functor $P$ sends $M$ to $C_{\mathcal B}(LM)$ and $a$ to $C_{\mathcal B}(L(a))$; it lands in $\mathcal B_c$ by hypothesis. The functor $D$ sends $N$ to $RN$ and $b$ to $R(b)$; it lands in $\mathcal A_c$ by the assumed preservation by $R$. Functoriality is inherited from the ambient functors. By [def-weil-linear-functor], their maps on morphisms satisfy $P(a+a')=P(a)+P(a')$, $P(ra)=rP(a)$, $D(b+b')=D(b)+D(b')$ and $D(rb)=rD(b)$. Thus both restricted functors are additive and $A$-linear.

source.place: Tag 099K, lemma-pushforward-derived-complete-adjoint, final Hom bijection; explicit abstract calculation supplied by the worker

proof.text: For $M\in\mathcal A_c$ and $N\in\mathcal B_c$, put $q_{M,N}(t)=t\circ\kappa_{LM}$. Fullness identifies its domain with $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal B}(C_{\mathcal B}(LM),N)$. The assumed universal property, with $X=LM$ and complete target $Y=N$, says precisely that $q_{M,N}$ is bijective; it does not require $LM$ to be complete. Bilinearity of composition [def-weil-linear-category] gives $q(t+t')=q(t)+q(t')$ and $q(rt)=rq(t)$. Its inverse is linear as well: applying the injective map $q$ to the proposed additivity or scalar equation for $q^{-1}$ gives the corresponding already proved equation for $q$.

source.place: Tag 099K, lemma-pushforward-derived-complete-adjoint, final Hom bijection; explicit abstract calculation supplied by the worker

proof.text: Write $h_{X,Y}$ for the specified ordinary adjunction bijection. Its unit formula [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection] is $h_{X,Y}(s)=R(s)\circ\eta_X$. Consequently $h(s+s')=h(s)+h(s')$ and $h(rs)=rh(s)$, by the linearity of $R$ [def-weil-linear-functor] and bilinearity of composition [def-weil-linear-category]. It is bijective by the given adjunction, and its inverse is linear by applying its injectivity to the two linearity equations. The same adjunction convention gives naturality in both variables and $h^{-1}_{RN,N}(1_{RN})=\varepsilon_N$.

source.place: Tag 099K, lemma-pushforward-derived-complete-adjoint, final Hom bijection; explicit abstract calculation supplied by the worker

proof.text: Define $\Phi_{M,N}=h_{M,N}\circ q_{M,N}$, using fullness and $DN=RN$ to identify the target Hom set. Steps 2 and 3 make it an $A$-linear bijection. For $a:M'\to M$, $b:N\to N'$ and $t:PM\to N$, naturality of $\kappa$ gives $P(a)\circ\kappa_{LM'}=\kappa_{LM}\circ L(a)$, whence $$q_{M',N'}(b\circ t\circ P(a))=b\circ q_{M,N}(t)\circ L(a).$$ Apply the two naturality laws for $h$ from step 3 to obtain $$\Phi_{M',N'}(b\circ t\circ P(a))=D(b)\circ\Phi_{M,N}(t)\circ a.$$ This is naturality in both variables, including each separately by setting the other arrow equal to an identity.

source.place: Tag 099K, lemma-pushforward-derived-complete-adjoint, final Hom bijection; explicit abstract calculation supplied by the worker

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection] with $F=P$, $G=D$ and the natural bijections $\Psi=\Phi$ constructed in step 4. Its hypotheses are exactly the two naturality identities just proved and bijectivity from steps 2 and 3. It produces $P\dashv D$ with precisely this Hom bijection, natural unit $\eta^c_M=\Phi_{M,PM}(1_{PM})$ and natural counit $\varepsilon^c_N=\Phi_{DN,N}^{-1}(1_{DN})$, and both triangle identities. Thus this application fixes the adjunction by the displayed composite bijection.

source.place: Tag 0037, definition-adjoint, natural Hom bijections and the following unit/counit formulas; explicit specialization to the supplied reflector

proof.text: Evaluate the unit formula of step 5. Since $q_{M,PM}(1_{PM})=\kappa_{LM}$, the ordinary adjunct formula of step 3 gives $$\eta^c_M=h_{M,PM}(\kappa_{LM})=R(\kappa_{LM})\circ\eta_M.$$ Its target is $R(C_{\mathcal B}(LM))=DPM$, which lies in $\mathcal A_c$ by the preservation hypothesis. Fullness makes this equality an equality of the required ambient morphisms.

source.place: Tag 099K, lemma-pushforward-derived-complete-adjoint, final Hom bijection; explicit abstract calculation supplied by the worker

proof.text: For the counit, step 5 says $h_{RN,N}(q_{DN,N}(\varepsilon^c_N))=1_{RN}$. Applying $h_{RN,N}^{-1}$ and the ordinary counit identity from step 3 gives $$\varepsilon^c_N\circ\kappa_{LRN}=q_{DN,N}(\varepsilon^c_N)=\varepsilon_N.$$ Here $RN\in\mathcal A_c$ by hypothesis, and $N\in\mathcal B_c$ ensures the bijection defining $q_{DN,N}$ exists. Its injectivity also shows that this equation characterizes the counit uniquely. For every $t:PM\to N$, the defining equality $\Phi_{M,N}(t)=h_{M,N}(t\circ\kappa_{LM})$ is exactly the asserted agreement of ordinary and completed adjuncts. No inverse of $\kappa_{LM}$ has been used.
